title: Insider Trading and Unauthorised Use or Disclosure of Confidential Information Policy and Guidelines (Rev 1.0) with Exhibit B Supplemental Policy on Section 16 Compliance Program
date_effective: May 2010 (Policy dated May 2010 per Exhibit A; document saved 6 November 2010)

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: All ResMed employees globally. 'Employee' expressly includes the Employee's spouse, children, relatives in the same household, any corporation or business entity controlled by the Employee and any trust in which the Employee is trustee or has a beneficial or pecuniary interest. Subject to confidentiality, the Trading Window (section 5, addressee not expressly limited), Rule 10b5-1 plan pre-approval and the Acknowledgement Form.

tiers.name: Insiders
tiers.description: Any Employee who may have access to material non-public information about ResMed, its customers, suppliers or counterparties; automatically classified if they have access to global financial information or revenue comprising 50% of global revenue, attend management meetings where global revenue is discussed, or have access to a combination of SBU revenue over 50% of global revenue. Sections 4.1 to 4.5 (insider trading, waiting period, tipping, stop-loss orders, speculative transactions including puts, calls and short sales) apply to Insiders and their household members, controlled entities and trusts.

tiers.name: Specified Persons
tiers.description: ResMed directors, executive officers, members of senior management and other persons identified from time to time by the Global General Counsel. Must obtain pre-approval from the Global General Counsel (or CFO in his absence) for any transaction involving ResMed Securities, including option exercise, purchase, sale, gift, loan, pledge, hedge, contribution to a trust or any other transfer or acquisition.

tiers.name: Section 16 Persons
tiers.description: Directors and executive officers of ResMed Inc. and other persons identified by the Global General Counsel who are subject to Section 16 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. In addition to the Policy, subject to the Supplemental Policy on Section 16 Compliance Program: Forms 3, 4 and 5 reporting, short-swing profit recovery under Section 16(b), Rule 144 sale restrictions, broker instructions and a year-end pre-clearance representation. Reporting and 16(b) extend to household family members and trusts, corporations or partnerships the person controls.

windows.start_anchor: one (1) full trading day following the date of public disclosure of the financial results for the prior fiscal quarter or year
windows.end_anchor: the later of (i) the last day of the three (3) calendar week period following the opening of the trading window or (ii) the last day of the second month of the fiscal quarter

windows.start_anchor: day after the trading window closes
windows.end_anchor: one full trading day after public disclosure of the next quarterly or annual financial results

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: No express ad hoc blackout power. The Global General Counsel, CEO or CFO may amend or supplement the Policy at any time with immediate effect (8.1), and the Global General Counsel (or CFO) may withhold pre-approval in his discretion for Specified Persons (6.1). Confidentiality of any such restriction is not addressed.

rules.detail: Buying or selling puts or calls on ResMed Securities is named as a speculative transaction and prohibited outright for Insiders (which in practice includes all directors and executive officers). No venue limit and no vesting-state carve-out, so both legs of a collar are banned. Section 5.1 states there are no exceptions beyond the five listed, none of which cover options.
rules.evidence: You are prohibited from engaging in any speculative transactions involving ResMed Securities, including: Buying or selling puts or calls on ResMed Securities; or Short sales (which are illegal for executive officers and directors).

rules.detail: The puts and calls ban is addressed to Insiders. Employees who are not Insiders and not Specified Persons face only the insider trading law, the Trading Window (if read as applying to all Employees) and the Rule 10b5-1 pre-approval requirement; ResMed Securities expressly include options, futures, calls, puts and warrants so the window applies to them.
rules.evidence: As an Insider, the following sections 4.1 through 4.5 apply to you

rules.detail: A 'hedge' is expressly listed as a transaction a Specified Person may engage in only with pre-approval from the Global General Counsel (or CFO), requested at least two business days ahead and granted only for a precise period at the approver's discretion. Because puts and calls are banned under 4.5, only non-option hedges (e.g. a forward or swap) could realistically be approved, and approval may be withheld for Section 16(b), Rule 144 or adverse publicity reasons.
rules.evidence: who wish to engage in any transaction involving ResMed Securities (including any option exercise, stock purchase, stock sale, gift, loan, pledge, hedge, contribution to a trust, or any other transfer or acquisition), must first obtain pre-approval of the transaction from the Global General Counsel, or the Chief Financial Officer in his absence.

rules.detail: Option-based hedging (purchased puts, written calls, collars) is banned for Insiders as speculative. Hedging by other instruments is not addressed for Insiders who are not Specified Persons.
rules.evidence: Buying or selling puts or calls on ResMed Securities

rules.detail: Collars, prepaid forwards, swaps and other monetisation structures are not named. A collar is caught by the puts and calls ban (4.5) and any other structure by the Specified Person pre-approval list (loan, pledge, hedge, any other transfer).
Short sales are named as speculative transactions and prohibited for Insiders; the Policy notes they are illegal for executive officers and directors (Section 16(c)).
rules.evidence: Short sales (which are illegal for executive officers and directors).

rules.detail: A 'loan' of ResMed Securities is listed among the transactions requiring Global General Counsel pre-approval; no outright ban.
rules.evidence: (including any option exercise, stock purchase, stock sale, gift, loan, pledge, hedge, contribution to a trust, or any other transfer or acquisition)

rules.detail: CFDs are not named. A CFD over ResMed stock is a speculative transaction involving ResMed Securities of the same character as the named puts, calls and short sales and would fall within the 4.5 ban.
rules.evidence: You are prohibited from engaging in any speculative transactions involving ResMed Securities

rules.detail: Margin loans are not named. A margin loan involves a pledge of ResMed Securities, which is a listed transaction requiring Global General Counsel pre-approval for Specified Persons. Not addressed for other Employees.
rules.evidence: gift, loan, pledge, hedge, contribution to a trust, or any other transfer or acquisition

rules.detail: A pledge of ResMed Securities is expressly a transaction requiring pre-approval from the Global General Counsel (or CFO); there is no prohibition on pledging.
rules.evidence: (including any option exercise, stock purchase, stock sale, gift, loan, pledge, hedge, contribution to a trust, or any other transfer or acquisition)

rules.detail: Borrowing against ResMed Securities is not named as such but the pledge securing the loan requires pre-approval; approval is discretionary and may be withheld where the transaction could cause adverse publicity or Section 16(b) exposure. No forced-sale, margin-call or disclosure provisions.
rules.evidence: Approval for a proposed transaction may be withheld by the Global General Counsel (or Chief Financial Officer in his absence), in his discretion, if ... the transaction could result in adverse publicity or have a material adverse impact on trading in ResMed Securities or ResMed

rules.detail: No policy holding period. Section 16(b) short-swing profit recovery applies by law to any purchase and sale, or sale and purchase, within six months (highest sale matched with lowest purchase), and pre-approval may be withheld where a transaction could trigger 16(b) liability. Exempt transactions include gifts, approved option grants, in-the-money option exercises and employee benefit plan transactions.
rules.evidence: Section 16(b) requires ResMed to recover any deemed profit resulting from any sale and purchase, or purchase and sale, by a Section 16 Person within a six-month period. It makes no difference how long the shares were held or whether the Section 16 person was in possession of material non-public information at the time of the trades.

clearance.approver: Global General Counsel (or Chief Financial Officer in his absence); disagreements referred to the Audit Committee of the Board for final resolution
clearance.evidence: A request for pre-approval should be submitted to the Global General Counsel (or CFO in his absence) at least two (2) business days in advance of the proposed transaction. ... Clearance, when given, will be only for the precise period specified.

clearance.approver: Global General Counsel (or Chief Financial Officer in his absence), applying additional Section 16(b), Form 4 notice and Rule 144 considerations
clearance.post_trade_to: Global General Counsel (broker reports quantity and price); SEC Form 4 prepared by the office of the Global General Counsel
clearance.post_trade_deadline: broker report promptly on the day of execution; Form 4 filed no later than the second business day after the transaction date; year-end written representation that all transactions were pre-cleared
clearance.evidence: Section 16 Persons are required to instruct their broker who handles trades in ResMed stock to: verify with our Global General Counsel that the proposed trade was pre-cleared by ResMed in advance of entering any trading order for ResMed stock; ... report to our Global General Counsel the quantity and price of any trade promptly on the day of execution of the trade.

clearance.approver: Global General Counsel pre-approval required only to implement, amend or terminate a qualified Rule 10b5-1 plan
clearance.evidence: Any person who wishes to implement, amend or terminate a qualified Rule 10b5-1 plan must first have the plan (or any amendment or proposal to terminate) pre-approved by the Global General Counsel.

short_term.basis: statutory Section 16(b): any purchase and sale or sale and purchase within six months, highest-priced sale matched with lowest-priced purchase regardless of order; extends to six months after ceasing to be a Section 16 Person
carve_outs: other transactions under employee benefit plans
short_term.evidence: Under SEC rules, certain transactions, including gifts, approved option grants, in-the-money option exercises, and other transactions under employee benefit plans, are considered "exempt transactions" under Section 16(b) and do not give rise to profit recovery.

exceptions.evidence: the exercise of stock options where cash is paid for the exercise price and tax withholding obligation, and the stock acquired upon exercise is held by the Employee

exceptions.approver: Global General Counsel pre-approves the plan, its amendment or termination
exceptions.evidence: the sale or purchase of ResMed Securities pursuant to a qualified Rule 10b5-1 plan
the ongoing purchase of shares pursuant to our Employee Stock Purchase Plan
sales of shares acquired under our Employee Stock Purchase Plan and sold in compliance with and under our Quick Sale Program

financing.price_trigger_guidance: Insiders may not place stop-loss orders or any other limit orders involving ResMed Securities except under a qualified Rule 10b5-1 plan (4.4); cleared orders at a given price must be confined to the clearance period and stopped if the person comes into possession of material non-public information (6.1).
financing_disclosure: Section 16 Persons: every transaction in ResMed Securities including derivative securities is reported to the SEC on Form 4 within two business days of the transaction date, prepared by the office of the Global General Counsel under power of attorney (Exhibit B 10.1, 10.3).
Section 16 Persons: broker must report the quantity and price of any trade to the Global General Counsel promptly on the day of execution (Exhibit B 10.5).
Section 16 Persons (excluding 10% stockholders): written representation at each fiscal year-end that all transactions during the year were pre-cleared (Exhibit B 10.3).

external_documents: Policies on the form and terms of qualified Rule 10b5-1 plans adopted by the Global General Counsel
ResMed Employee Stock Purchase Plan and Quick Sale Program
Section 16 power of attorney in favour of the Global General Counsel and CFO
exemption_authority: None for the trading window: 'Apart from these five exceptions ... there shall be no exceptions to the foregoing prohibitions' (5.1), and no hardship or court-order relief exists. The Global General Counsel (or CFO) exercises discretionary pre-approval for Specified Persons, with the Audit Committee giving final resolution of a disputed request and management unable to overrule a refusal (6.1). The Global General Counsel, CEO or CFO may amend or supplement the Policy at any time with immediate effect (8.1).
jurisdiction_overlays: US federal securities law: Rule 10b-5 insider trading, Rule 10b5-1 plans, Section 16(a) Forms 3/4/5, Section 16(b) short-swing profit recovery, Section 16(c) short sale ban, Rule 144 affiliate sale restrictions (Form 144, volume limits, broker's transaction)
NYSE primary listing; Australian insider trading law noted as similar for ASX-traded shares (2.1)

bespoke_clauses.clause: You are prohibited from engaging in any speculative transactions involving ResMed Securities, including: Buying or selling puts or calls on ResMed Securities
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar is a purchased put and a written call, so both option legs are expressly prohibited for Insiders regardless of whether the shares are vested, the venue is OTC, or the purpose is protective rather than speculative.

bespoke_clauses.clause: any transaction involving ResMed Securities (including any option exercise, stock purchase, stock sale, gift, loan, pledge, hedge, contribution to a trust, or any other transfer or acquisition), must first obtain pre-approval of the transaction from the Global General Counsel
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Pledging shares to the bank and any non-option hedge are clearable transactions for Specified Persons, so the loan leg is possible with approval even though the option legs are not; approval must be sought at least two business days ahead.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Approval for a proposed transaction may be withheld ... if ... the transaction could result in adverse publicity or have a material adverse impact on trading in ResMed Securities or ResMed; for persons subject to Section 16 ... the transaction could result in liability to the Specified Person under the short-swing rules of Section 16(b); or sufficient advance notice had not been given to allow preparation and review of a Form 4
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even a permitted pledge or hedge can be refused on reputational or Section 16(b) grounds, and a refusal cannot be overruled by management.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Clearance, when given, will be only for the precise period specified. ... It is incumbent on the Specified Person to stop any such order that extends beyond the permitted period, or when the Specified Person comes into possession of material non-public information.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any cleared transaction must be executed within the stated period and abandoned if inside information arises, so a multi-step financing cannot rely on a standing approval.

bespoke_clauses.clause: You are prohibited from placing any "stop loss" orders or any other "limit order" involving ResMed Securities, except pursuant to a qualified Rule 10b5-1 plan
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Price-triggered mechanics such as knock-outs, automatic top-up sales or lender liquidation instructions could be characterised as prohibited stop-loss or limit orders unless housed in a pre-approved 10b5-1 plan.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Apart from these five exceptions, listed in a through e of this paragraph, there shall be no exceptions to the foregoing prohibitions.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no hardship, court-order or lender-enforcement relief, so any sale or settlement outside a trading window is a breach.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Total sales of ResMed common stock by a covered individual for any three-month period may not exceed the greater of: (i) 1% of the total number of outstanding shares ... or (ii) the average weekly reported volume ... The shares must be sold either in a "broker's transaction" or in a transaction directly with a "market maker."
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Physical delivery of shares to the bank on exercise or enforcement by a director or executive officer is an affiliate sale subject to Rule 144 volume limits, manner-of-sale rules and Form 144 filing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: require our Section 16 Persons to report all transactions involving ResMed Securities (including options, warrants, and other "derivative securities") to the SEC. Almost all transactions must be reported within two business days after the transaction date.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any derivative or pledge-related transaction by a director or executive officer becomes public on Form 4 within two business days and may be matched against other trades within six months for short-swing profit disgorgement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: you could receive permission to buy a security, but later be refused permission to sell it (at least temporarily). These situations are frequently beyond the control of ResMed, and could lock you into an unwanted investment for a considerable period of time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: ResMed disclaims responsibility if a later clearance to sell or unwind is refused, so the executive bears the liquidity risk of being unable to settle or restructure.

bespoke_clauses.clause: An Employee includes an Employee's spouse, children, or relatives in the same household; corporation or other business entity controlled by an Employee, or trust in which the Employee acts as trustee or has a beneficial or pecuniary interest.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Structuring a collar or loan through a family trust or controlled company does not escape the puts and calls ban or the pre-approval requirement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: this policy may be amended or supplemented at any time by our Global General Counsel, Chief Executive Officer or Chief Financial Officer and that any such amendments or supplements will become effective immediately.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The rules governing an outstanding financing can change without notice or Board process during the life of the arrangement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: You will only be allowed to purchase or sell ResMed Securities during a trading window period commencing one (1) full trading day following the date of our public disclosure of the financial results
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Section 5 does not say whether it binds all Employees or only Insiders, but for directors and executives it plainly applies and the Global General Counsel may refuse clearance whenever the window is not in effect.

bespoke_clauses.clause: In accordance with Listing Rule 12.9, which is due to take effect from 1 January 2011, we submit a copy of the Company's current Insider Trading Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the December 2010 lodgement of a May 2010 policy; the current ResMed policy should be checked before relying on these terms.

summary: A funded collar is not possible in its standard form for ResMed directors and executive officers. Section 4.5 expressly prohibits Insiders (any Employee with access to material non-public information, which captures all directors and executive officers and their household members, controlled entities and trusts) from buying or selling puts or calls on ResMed Securities as speculative transactions, so both option legs are banned regardless of vesting or venue, with no hardship or discretionary exemption other than the power of the Global General Counsel, CEO or CFO to amend the Policy. The loan leg is not banned: a pledge, loan or hedge is a transaction that Specified Persons (directors, executive officers, senior management) may undertake with discretionary pre-approval from the Global General Counsel (or CFO), requested at least two business days ahead, inside a trading window that opens one full trading day after quarterly results and runs at least three weeks, and valid only for the precise period specified. A non-option hedge such as a forward or swap could in theory be pre-approved but faces Section 16(b) six-month short-swing matching, Rule 144 affiliate sale limits, Form 4 disclosure within two business days and the ban on stop-loss and limit orders outside a Rule 10b5-1 plan. Note that this is a 2010-vintage policy and current terms should be verified.
